req.title: Login required for delete
req.statement: The system shall redirect anonymous users to /auth/login when they POST /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: R-FLASKR-014 requires that anonymous (unauthenticated) users who POST to /<id>/delete are redirected to /auth/login. The test suite must cover: (1) positive case — anonymous POST triggers 302 redirect to /auth/login; (2) negative case — authenticated user can POST and gets a successful redirect (not blocked); (3) boundary case — POST to a non-existent post id while anonymous still redirects to /auth/login (auth check fires before post-existence check). Additional cases cover the exact redirect location string, state transition from anonymous to authenticated, and decision table covering both auth states. Mutation resilience is achieved by asserting exact status codes (302 vs 200/403/404), exact Location header values, and testing both sides of the auth guard condition.

tests.name: test_anonymous_post_delete_redirects_to_login
preconditions: App is initialised with test database containing pre-loaded rows
No user is logged in (anonymous session)
Post id=1 exists in the database (author_id=5, James)
actions: Create Flask test client with no session
trace: R-FLASKR-014: anonymous POST /<id>/delete must redirect to /auth/login
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os

def test_anonymous_post_delete_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_anonymous_post_delete_redirects_to_login()

tests.name: test_authenticated_user_post_delete_not_redirected_to_login
preconditions: App is initialised with test database containing pre-loaded rows
User Rahul (id=1) is logged in with password 'stone'
Post id=2 exists and is authored by Rahul (author_id=1)
actions: Log in as Rahul via POST /auth/login
expected: Login response status code is exactly 302
Delete response status code is exactly 302
Delete Location header is exactly / (redirects to index, not to /auth/login)
trace: R-FLASKR-014: authenticated users must NOT be redirected to /auth/login on delete
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os

def test_authenticated_user_post_delete_not_redirected_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/2/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'
    assert r.headers['Location'] != '/auth/login'

test_authenticated_user_post_delete_not_redirected_to_login()

tests.name: test_state_transition_logout_then_delete_redirects_to_login
preconditions: App is initialised with test database containing pre-loaded rows
User Anjali (id=2) logs in, then logs out, becoming anonymous again
Post id=7 exists (author_id=2, Anjali)
actions: Log in as Anjali via POST /auth/login
POST to /7/delete in the now-anonymous state
expected: Login response status code is exactly 302
Logout response status code is exactly 302
Delete response status code is exactly 302
trace: R-FLASKR-014: after logout the session is cleared; subsequent POST /<id>/delete must redirect to /auth/login
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os

def test_state_transition_logout_then_delete_redirects_to_login():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    login_r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Anjali', 'password': 'cloud'})
    assert login_r.status_code == 302
    logout_r = client.get('/auth/logout')
    assert logout_r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/7/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login'

test_state_transition_logout_then_delete_redirects_to_login()

from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os

def test_anonymous_post_delete_multiple_post_ids_all_redirect():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    for post_id in [1, 10, 20]:
        r = client.post(f'/{post_id}/delete')
        assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 for post {post_id}, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.headers['Location'] == '/auth/login', f'Expected /auth/login for post {post_id}'

test_anonymous_post_delete_multiple_post_ids_all_redirect()
